title: Cream puff, eclair, custard or cream filled, iced

content.title: About
content.content: A cream puff (eclair) is a small pastry made from light choux dough, filled with custard or pastry cream and topped with a glaze. The dough is created from water, butter, flour and eggs, while the filling typically consists of vanilla custard, pastry cream, or a flavored cream, sometimes enriched with fruit.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Eclairs originated in France in the 17th century; the name comes from the French word “éclair”, meaning “lightning”, because they disappear quickly from the plate.
Traditional filling is pastry cream, but modern recipes often use custard, whipped cream, or mascarpone‑based creams.
Glazes can be chocolate, sugar, or fruit‑based, allowing a wide range of flavor combinations.
Eclairs are a staple in patisseries and cafés, served as individual desserts or as part of a dessert platter.
In Russia, a similar pastry is called “profiterole”, frequently served with chocolate sauce.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: Both the choux dough and the cream contain eggs, providing high‑quality protein.

items.title: Calcium and vitamin D
items.content: Dairy‑based fillings supply calcium, essential for bone and teeth health.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: Eclairs deliver quick energy from the carbohydrates in the dough and the fats in the cream.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs and dairy contribute B2, B12 and other B‑vitamins involved in metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants in chocolate glaze
items.content: When dark chocolate glaze is used, it provides flavonoids with antioxidant properties.

items.title: Egg and dairy allergies
items.content: Eclairs can trigger allergic reactions in individuals sensitive to eggs or lactose.

items.title: High sugar and fat content
items.content: Glaze and cream often contain significant amounts of sugar and saturated fat, which may contribute to weight gain if consumed frequently.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: One cream puff can contain 150–250 kcal, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Trans‑fat presence
items.content: Using margarine instead of butter in the dough may introduce trans fats.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve cream puffs at room temperature; they can be enjoyed as a standalone dessert or alongside coffee or tea. For extra flair, add fresh berries, toasted nuts, or a dusting of powdered sugar.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cream puffs in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Allow them to come to room temperature before serving. They can be frozen for up to 2 months if wrapped tightly in plastic film.
